metadata.change_reason: Add mandatory release priority grading rule (P0/P1/P2) following Big Tech (Google) PRD standards.

rules.statement: Every feature specification in the PRD must trace back to at least one user story
Every user story declared in the User Story set must be mapped and implemented by at least one feature specification in the PRD (100% story coverage). Zero orphan stories permitted.
Every declared user persona must have substantive feature specifications supporting their primary jobs and operational workflows across all tiers.
Every feature specification must define at least 3 detailed business rules (>= 20 chars each), >= 2 preconditions, and >= 2 postconditions. One-sentence stubs are strictly rejected.

Every feature specification must define concrete Input parameters (>= 1 with type, required flag, validation constraints), Output artifacts (>= 1 with type and business description), and Feature-level Error Cases (>= 1 with error code, trigger condition, user feedback, and recovery action).

Every feature specification must declare explicit data dependencies with verified closed-world source attribution (INTERNAL_FEATURE, COLD_START_SEED, EXTERNAL_API, USER_INPUT). All internal producer references must resolve to valid feature IDs, strictly eliminating dangling preconditions.
Every module declared in Information Architecture must be covered by at least one concrete feature specification.
Core business entities must possess explicit state machine definitions with zero isolated deadlock states and explicit transition triggers, conditions, and actions
Must fully specify system/business exception recovery strategies and Tracking Plan analytics instrumentation
Must fully specify performance, security, reliability/availability, privacy, and compliance requirements.
Strictly prohibit unverified placeholders such as TBD or Pending across all PRD sections
PRD must strictly focus on behavioral contracts and business rules, prohibiting code-level SQL DDL or frontend implementation details
PRD must explicitly declare a target domain_profile (mobile, desktop, backend, iot_hardware, or hybrid) and formulate domain-specific non-functional and behavioral specifications.

PRD business rules must strictly adhere to RFC 2119 normative keywords (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHOULD, MAY), eliminating vague expressions like 'as appropriate', 'roughly', or 'depending on circumstances'.

PRD authoring strictly prohibits standalone hallucination without upstream dependencies. Valid user stories (Stage 03) and 5W1H requirements (Stage 01) must be physically grounded in the project context.

Every feature input parameter must define an explicit, non-empty validation_rule (>= 5 chars). Every error recovery action must provide substantive, actionable instructions (>= 10 chars). Superficial one-word placeholders are strictly vetoed.
Every feature specification in the PRD must be explicitly graded with a release priority (P0, P1, or P2). P0 features (launch blockers) must form an end-to-end viable backbone.

All PRD IDs (MOD-xxx, FEAT-xxx, ERR_xxx) must be strictly formatted, globally unique, feature IDs must bind to their module namespace, and feature sequences must be 1-based monotonically increasing without gaps.

All human-readable narrative and documentation must enforce clean typography standards: wrapping technical identifiers, parameters, and error codes in backticks, and ensuring comfortable Markdown visual hierarchy.
